title: Focus lattice — weekly rituals & micro-KPIs
content:
Notes to self — lightweight, actionable.

Context: personal weekly scratchpad for tracking small wins, experiments and blockers that feed into my quarterly OKRs. Keep short, do one tidy update each Tue morning.

Quick metrics (this week snapshot)
- Deep work hours logged: 12.5h (target 18h)
- PRs merged: 3 (target 5)
- Review turnaround median: 22h (target <24h)
- Customer debug sessions: 1 (target 2)
- Small experiments launched: 1 (prefix-cache heuristics A/B)
- Energy score (subjective 1-5): 3

Micro-KPIs I actually care about (one-liners)
- Reduce review cycle time to <24h for priority PRs (measure via PR labels).
- Raise deep work share to 20h/week by locking mornings.
- Get at least one measurable perf improvement experiment into canary per sprint.
- Save $/token on low-risk routes via quantize+cache combo (proof: perf/cost delta).

This week's wins
- Pulled in prefix-cache experiment and got a 6% token-cost drop on the sample workload (local run, need stage run).
- Wrote two small RFC comments on rollout safety for model fallback.
- Cleared backlog of small docs: rollout checklist + oncall notes.

Where I stalled / blockers
- Couldn't book the customer session; calendar conflict. Follow up with CS to reschedule.
- Team bandwidth low for the canary rollout; may need to re-prioritize latency-opt work.

Hypotheses / experiments for next week
1) Prefix-cache eviction policy tweak ({evict-oldest-kv: true}) will reduce average tokens generated per request by ~2-4% for short prompts. Test: stage canary for 48h vs control. Success metric: delta in tokens-per-request and 95p latency impact <5%.
2) Pomodoro morning lock (9–11am) increases deep work by 25% and reduces PR open time. Measurement: block time logged + PR merge count.

Concrete to-dos (priority-ordered)
- [ ] Push stage canary for prefix-cache policy tweak, link ENG-4321 (owner: me) — due Thu
- [ ] Send invite for customer debug (options: Tue/Wed next week) — due Wed
- [ ] Draft short playbook entry: "How to open a canary for perf-sensitive routes" — due Fri
- [ ] Add review auto-assign label on PRs to reduce handoff delays — pair with Arjun — due Mon

Calendar/timeboxing (high level)
- Mornings (9:00–11:00) = deep work focus (no meetings).
- Midday (13:00–15:00) = async work (reviews, docs).
- Late day (16:00–17:30) = sync / operational (standups, calls).

Retro notes (quick, rough)
- What went well: small experiments shipped faster than expected when I paired with Arjun — pair programming unblock works.
- What didn't: fragmented mornings from ad-hoc meetings — need stronger guards and calendar etiquette.
- One thing to stop: accepting meeting invites without a clear agenda/timebox.
- One thing to start: 2x/week "no meetings" window protected on my calendar.

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: canary causes regressions mid-day when traffic patterns change. Mitigation: automatic fallback and tighter SLO thresholds during ramp (monitoring alert hook).
- Risk: experiment PRs drift into feature creep. Mitigation: split into micro-PR + feature follow-up.

Short draft for next OKR check-in (1 paragraph)
Goal: Improve serving efficiency and developer velocity for the serving-runtime team. Key results I influence this quarter: reduce cost-per-token on common low-compute routes by 8%, decrease latency tail for short prompts by 10%, and cut review-to-merge time for small perf patches to <24h. Weekly plan: ship one experiment to stage every sprint, protect deep work mornings, and keep a rolling 3-item list of priority PRs.

Misc scratch (ideas, one-liners, noise)
- Try small reward for reviewers (emoji + short note) to encourage faster turnarounds.
- Consider an "experiment dry-run" checklist before canarying to reduce oncall noise.
- Note: check quantization bits impact on embedding routes — might be different trade-off.
- Bookmark: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/987 (local perf notes)

Done items (since last week)
- prefix-cache prototype (local bench)
- rollout checklist draft
- two RFC comments

Open questions to answer in the Tuesday sync
- Can SRE support a 48h canary with incremental traffic ramp? Who needs to be on-call?
- Do we want a separate label for "perf-priority" to route reviews faster?

End-of-week quick scorecard (fill Fri)
- Deep work hours vs target: __ / __
- PRs merged vs target: __ / __
- Experiment progress: on-track / delayed / blocked

Notes to self: keep language short in updates, emphasize measurable outcomes, and when in doubt pick the smaller experiment.
